title: Cypress Reference
description: A quick reminder of the ideas and examples in the Cypress lessons. Open the linked lesson when you need more help.

entries.name: Meet the Cypress runner
entries.summary: Cypress runs browser checks as a chain of commands. This example starts with a blank local practice page.
notes: Serve a blank practice.html from your local frontend project and configure baseUrl first.

entries.name: Select a clear target
entries.summary: A stable data attribute can identify a control without tying a test to its visual style.
notes: A color class is often a fragile test selector because design changes it.

entries.name: Type into a field
entries.summary: type enters text and clear removes existing text. A final value check confirms the input received it.
notes: Cypress commands are queued; do not read their result like an immediate normal value.

entries.name: Click and check the effect
entries.summary: A click test needs an observable result. Here the button changes its own text.
notes: Do not consider a click alone proof of the business result.

entries.name: Retry an assertion
entries.summary: Cypress retries many queries and assertions until they pass or time out. Check a real condition instead of guessing a delay.
notes: Arbitrary cy.wait delays can make tests both slow and unreliable.

entries.name: Read a yielded value
entries.summary: then receives the value yielded by the previous command. This is how you inspect queued results.
notes: Do not assign cy.get to a variable and treat it as the DOM element.

entries.name: Work with checkboxes
entries.summary: check requests the checked state. It states intent more clearly than a toggle click.
notes: Check applies to checkboxes and radio buttons, not an arbitrary button.

entries.name: Select a dropdown value
entries.summary: select chooses a native option by value or text. Assert the stored value after the action.
notes: A custom popup is not a native select and needs different actions.

entries.name: Count a collection
entries.summary: A query can find several elements. have.length checks how many the query found.
notes: A correct count does not guarantee correct item text.

entries.name: Intercept a request
entries.summary: intercept can supply a known network response. Set it up before the page sends the request.
notes: A mocked response tests the frontend contract, not a real server implementation.

entries.name: Keep tests independent
entries.summary: A test should set up the state it needs. Cypress test isolation helps avoid state leaking from a previous test.
notes: Do not rely on one test running before another to prepare data.

entries.name: Review failures and screenshots
entries.summary: A failed assertion tells you which expected condition was not met. Use the command log and screenshot to understand it.
notes: Do not hide a failure by deleting its assertion.
